text.p: Richard Scott resigned on Friday as chairman of Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., the giant for-profit hospital chain being investigated for fraud by federal regulators.
Resigning along with Scott, founder of the company, was President and Chief Operating Officer David Vandewater, the company said.
Half a dozen federal agencies are probing the operations of Columbia/HCA, examining Medicare-billing practices, home health-care operations, recruitment of physicians, and other matters.
Thomas Frist, Jr., vice chairman of the Columbia/HCA board, was named to succeed Scott as chairman and chief executive officer, the company said.

"Both executives (Scott and Vandewater) emphasized that throughout their tenure they have acted honorably and in the best interests of the company," Columbia/HCA said in a statement announcing the resignations.

Frist said in a statement, "Our board and management will be focusing on providing full cooperation with all governmental agencies. We will also ensure that all Columbia facilities and employees are in full compliance with the law."

Scott said in a statement, "Since founding Columbia, we have been dedicated to improving healthcare through a focus on quality care. At the same time, we have had a strong emphasis on creating value for shareholders.
"Though the decision to resign was an extremely difficult one, we consider it to be the ultimate demonstration of our commitment to Columbia's mission."
